newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close softer on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close softer on profit-taking.

text.p: French shares ended lower after a gust of profit-taking took the Paris bourse lower in late afternoon trading.
Traders said a slip in the dollar versus the mark, later corrected, sent a signal for investors to book profits on some of the market's recent strong rise.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 23.06 points or 0.85 percent at 2,686.15. The CAC-40 futures contract was down 19 points at 2,696 from Monday's close.
* French bonds end firm but off highs, pulled back by weaker U.S. Treasuries and Bunds.

* Lafarge falls 3.14 percent to 367.5 francs, weighed by profit-taking ahead of 1996 results due tomorrow. Analysts expect the building materials company will report profit lower than 1995, with net attributable gain of 1.9-2.0 billion francs against 2.35 billion in 1995.
* BNP drops 2.35 percent, hit by a newspaper report Axa-UAP plans to cut its holding in the bank. The stock rose strongly last week on the back of strong profits.
Brokers cite continuing row over Belgian plant closure.
* Total bucks trend, rises 0.43 percent, helped by a newspaper report Axa-UAP will sell half of Elf-Aquitaine stake to buy Total stock. Elf was down 0.69 percent at 578.
* Canal Plus also among rare risers, up 2.27 percent at 1,125. The broadcaster has been supported by hopes of a launch of a single Spanish digital television service.
* Among biggest falls were Cie Generale des Eaux, Eridania Beghin-Say, Legrand, Danone and Promodes -- all down over two percent.
* The government said after the close offers for the Thomson-CSF privatisation should be in by March 28 and it will pick the winner by June 30.

It earlier named Marcel Roulet as chairman of Thomson-CSF, to be work on its privatisation and put in an ex-Cie des Machines Bull executive, Thierry Breton, to head Thomson SA and to prepare the Multimedia subsidiary for privatisation.
* Castorama ends up 3.18 percent at 908, helped by hopes of stronger 1997 profit performance.
